stories.title: Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh City proposes curbs on gasoline, diesel vehicles from mid-2027
stories.summary: HANOI, Aug 26 - Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam's commercial hub, is proposing to gradually restrict gasoline- and diesel-powered vehicles from its downtown area from mid-2027 as part of a planned low-emission zone (LEZ), state-run Thanh Nien newspaper reported, citing city authorities.
article_sentences: Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam's commercial hub, is proposing to gradually restrict gasoline- and diesel-powered vehicles from its downtown area from mid-2027 as part of a planned low-emission zone (LEZ), state-run Thanh Nien newspaper reported, citing city authorities.
Under the proposal, the city would pilot the LEZ from July 2027 in its core downtown area and the new Thu Thiem urban area, which covers roughly 930 hectares (3.59 square miles), Thanh Nien reported.

After two years of piloting, the LEZ would expand to within the city's Ring Road 2 from early 2029, an area that already restricts heavy trucks and sleeper buses from the inner city during certain hours, it added.
The new timeline is later than a previous proposal, in which the implementation of the LEZ was set to begin in early 2026.
The revised plan adjusts the scope and some milestones to align with the launch of green transport infrastructure and give residents and businesses more time to switch vehicles.
Buses are the first group required to convert, and will need to use electricity or clean energy when entering the LEZ starting in 2027.
Motorcycle-taxi drivers and delivery riders would follow, while other categories such as taxis face later deadlines.
The proposal remains subject to further review before it is formally approved.

stories.title: Indonesia’s Destry says she will back growth policies if confirmed as central bank chief
stories.summary: Destry Damayanti, nominee for Indonesia's central bank governor, pledges to support growth, job creation, and financial stability while maintaining Bank Indonesia's independence. She aims to strengthen exchange-rate stabilisation with smart interventions and optimise monetary operations to ensure liquidity and policy effectiveness. Destry's confirmation is expected soon amid economic concerns, with her leadership seen as continuity after recent resignations and market instability. Destry Damayanti, the sole candidate nominated for Indonesia’s central bank governor, on Aug 26 told a vetting panel she will look to support growth and job creation while ensuring financial stability if she becomes Bank Indonesia’s chief. She also said synergy with other institutions would not reduce Bank Indonesia’s independence. Destry, 62, currently interim governor, is undergoing a “fit and proper” hearing in Parliament for the role, which could see her become the first woman to take the top job. It comes at a tumultuous time in Indonesia, with unease among businesses and investors about fiscal management, central bank autonomy, equity market transparency and the stewardship of the US$1.4 trillion (S$1.78 million) G-20 economy. “BI is not only tasked with maintaining the stability of the rupiah exchange rate, the stability of the payment system and the stability of the financial system, but also with implementing a policy mix that can create an economic environment conducive to real sector growth and job creation,” Destry told Parliament’s financial committee in her opening remarks. With Parliament dominated by parties allied with President Prabowo Subianto, senior deputy governor Destry is widely expected to be confirmed by legislators, who have not rejected a sitting president’s nominee for the post since 2008. Destry needs to pass a plenary vote before being appointed by the president. The committee’s decision on Destry is expected on Aug 27, with the interview process for the senior deputy chief slot expected later on Aug 26. Reuters had reported Destry was the frontrunner for the job and the Aug 10 announcement of her candidacy gave a boost to the rupiah, which has plunged amid capital outflows triggered by anxiety and perceptions of policymaking uncertainty.
